7 ways to be unrecognisable
by the end of the year
Learn to cook five real meals. One a week until you've got five you can make without a recipe. By December, you eat better, spend less, and dinner at your place becomes something people want.
Fix your morning. Same wake-up time every day, light first, coffee second, phone third. Two months of calm mornings changes your mood, your skin and how much you get done before noon.
Do one hard conversation you've been avoiding. The raise, the friend who owes you, the thing you never said. Most of the weight people carry comes from the talks they keep putting off.
Start a strength routine you can't fail. Push-ups, squats and planks, ten minutes, every day. No gym needed. Consistency beats intensity, and by December your body will show it.
Clean up your space. Clear the desk, fix the broken lamp, wash the curtains. A place that looks cared for changes how you feel in it, and how people see you when they come over.
Feed your head every day. Five minutes of history, art or science. By December you'll have a few hundred new things you actually understand, and it shows in how you talk.
slides.texte_sophia: Before: twenty minutes of scrolling every morning. After: five minutes on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. History, art, science. By December, it shows in how you talk.

slides.texte_overlay: Write down three goals and read them every Sunday. Not twenty. Three. People who look at their goals every week are the ones who are actually different by the end of the year.
